root_idea.summary: The lexical field joins wildness and untamedness with gathering, enclosing, and drawing things together.
root_idea.development: The possible underlying principle is cautiously described as gathering from around: game is collected toward a snare, while related developments include enclosing, withdrawal, and being moved or affected. These root-level connections do not make every development a meaning of every form.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quranic form is presented under the normalized lexical expression حاشا, represented in the Quranic text as حاشَ.

senses.definition: An expression of exoneration: far be Allah from this; Allah forbid.
senses.usage_conditions: Used in the Quranic construction حاشَ لِلَّهِ to declare Allah free from an attributed fault or unacceptable matter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To drive game or animals toward a snare or a person by coming around them; hence, to collect or draw them together.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used for driving game, sheep or goats, camels, and similar animals; it can also mean simply to collect or draw together.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To collect several things, or to collect much.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form II usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To turn aside from the place reached by the rain of lightning, whichever way it turns.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in the construction حاوش البرقَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To circumvent someone, or try to induce him to turn, incline, or yield, including by deceit or guile.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in contexts such as war, litigation, contention, or other attempts to influence someone indirectly.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To excite, incite, urge, or instigate someone to do something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative urging construction, including حاوشته عليه.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To withdraw, retire, or move away from people or a group.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used both with عن and with مِنْ in expressions of removal or withdrawal.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become forlorn of one’s husband, or become without a husband.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized usage applied to a woman separated from or bereft of her husband.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To feel or be moved with shame, shyness, or bashfulness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes an inward reaction of embarrassment or modesty.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take fright and flee; to be frightened at, averse from, or shrink from someone or something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The form can describe frightened withdrawal or aversion, including an animal’s response to being chided or driven.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be moved or affected by, and therefore to care about or regard, something or someone; in the negative, not to be moved or concerned.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Especially attested in the negative construction ما ينحاشُ من شيءٍ or من فلانٍ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become gathered together.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested of camels becoming collected into a group.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To encompass or surround; to place someone in the midst of a group; of game, to drive it from one party to another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The same enclosing image is used figuratively of blood surrounding or invading a state of purity from different sides.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An enclosure resembling a fenced holding-place; a court or enclosed space beside or within a house.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The enclosure sense is associated with the dialect of Iraq; the court sense is reported in Egyptian usage and may refer to a space surrounded by dwellings or walls.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Wild animals or game.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal use equating الحوش with الوحش.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Wild, untamed, undomesticated, uncivilized, unfamiliar, or unsociable.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to people and animals. Of camels, it can refer to wild or incompletely trained animals and is also associated in traditional accounts with camels of the jinn.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Acute or sharp in intellect.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression حوشيّ الفؤاد, literally describing the heart or mind.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Strange, uncouth, unusual, or difficult-to-understand speech; a rare or unfamiliar word or phrase.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to speech, a word, or an expression, in contrast with clear eloquence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Dark and terrible.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested as an epithet of night.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Wildness or unsociability of disposition; the quality of not mixing with others.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun describing the disposition of a person characterized as حوشيّ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Encompassed or surrounded.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Passive participial description of something placed within an enclosing group or boundary.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A matter in which there is sin.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexical use describing an act or affair involving wrongdoing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Shyness or bashfulness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun for the state of one who withdraws inwardly from a matter out of modesty.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A group or cluster of date palms.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A collective noun reported as having no singular form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To eat from the sides of food until it is consumed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of eating around the edges or sides of food.

cautions: The Quranic spelling حاشَ is presented under the normalized citation expression حاشا; grammatical analyses of this expression vary.
The proposed connection between the root and gathering is presented cautiously in the root-level discussion and is not used by itself to establish a Quranic form sense.
